newsitem.title: UK: Australia 1H 1996 sugar output sharply higher - ISO.
newsitem.headline: Australia 1H 1996 sugar output sharply higher - ISO.

text.p: Australia produced 309,309 tonnes of sugar in the first six months of 1996, sharply higher than the 90,957 tonnes turned out in the same period in 1995, the International Sugar Organization (ISO) said on Tuesday. The difference was mainly due to the amount of sugar produced in June, the first month of Australia's sugar campaign, which runs to December.

Production in June 1996 reached 302,890 tonnes compared with just 90,957 tonnes in the same month a year earlier. But exports for the first six months of this year were lower than in 1995, the ISO said.

Canada, Malaysia and New Zealand were Australia's main sugar buyers for both periods under review. But Japan and Korea took significantly more Australian sugar over the 1995 period than in 1996, accounting for the difference in total sales.
Sugar exports for this year's January/June period amounted to 764,912 tonnes, against 1.16 million tonnes for the first half of 1995, the data showed.
